# Continual-ARC task-c4b91aa4: replicate a template across divider panels

Use when a grid is partitioned by complete straight divider lines (often color 6) into congruent rectangular panels, one panel contains a colored pattern, and the other panels are mostly a uniform blank/background (observed as 1). Copy the template panel's contents into each corresponding panel, preserving the divider lines.

## Validated behavior
- Demo: 5×9 input with a full vertical divider column of 3 at column 4. The 5×4 panel to the left was uniform 7 (blank), while the right 5×4 panel held a pattern. Output copied the right pattern into the left panel, preserving the divider. Pattern pixels were copied exactly, including its 7-valued cells; this is panel replication rather than recoloring.
- Fresh test: 11×13 input with full horizontal divider row 3 and full vertical divider column 6 (both color 6), forming four 3×6 panels with 3×6 content spans. The top-left panel contained a 3×6 template; remaining panels were blank 1s. Output tiled the exact 3×6 template into all four panels, preserving both divider lines. Accepted.

## Procedure
1. Find complete divider rows/columns and treat them as immutable boundaries.
2. Identify congruent panel dimensions and locate the populated template panel.
3. Repeat the template panel's entire cell matrix into every other aligned panel, including template-colored/background cells; do not merely stamp non-background marks or recolor the blanks.
4. Preserve divider cells and validate dimensions and panel alignment before submitting.

Do not assume this rule for arbitrary grids without the full-divider/congruent-panel structure.
